Why this matters

A hotel acquisition combines a real estate transaction with an operating business. Roof condition, hot-water equipment, guestroom access, and deferred maintenance affect the building review, while franchise requirements introduce a separate renovation question.

Choose the company whose written scope answers your acquisition and financing questions. A recognizable name does not establish which rooms, systems, documents, or specialist investigations your particular assignment includes.

For a 2026 hotel purchase, distinguish physical-condition findings from operating forecasts and brand requirements. Each informs the investment decision, but none substitutes for the others.

What makes the best hotel inspection company

Judge hotel property condition assessment providers against these criteria before comparing proposals:

  • Hotel-specific scope: The proposal addresses guestrooms, public areas, back-of-house spaces, building systems, and site improvements where applicable.
  • Useful capital planning: Findings distinguish immediate repair concerns from longer-term replacement planning and explain estimating assumptions.
  • Defined access: The agreement identifies accessible areas, representative sampling, escort requirements, and restrictions caused by occupancy.
  • Specialist boundaries: Structural, environmental, elevator, fire-protection, and other specialist work is clearly included, excluded, or separately commissioned.
  • Transaction fit: The reporting requirements match the buyer, lender, ownership entity, and intended users.
  • Accountability: The proposal identifies responsibility for the site visit, report preparation, technical review, and follow-up questions.

Do not rank providers by a delivery promise alone. A fast report with unresolved access restrictions still leaves the buyer with unanswered questions.

How to scope a hotel PCA before selecting a company

Use the same assignment brief for every shortlisted firm. For a 2026 acquisition, organize that brief around four decisions:

  1. Define reliance: Identify the buyer, lender, intended report users, required standard, and transaction deadline.
  2. Plan access: Specify guestroom sampling, occupied areas, roof access, equipment rooms, escorts, and inaccessible spaces.
  3. Set priorities: Request clear treatment of urgent concerns, near-term repairs, and longer-term replacements.
  4. Assign follow-up: Identify who authorizes specialist investigations and who resolves unanswered questions before closing.

This sequence keeps a proposal comparison focused on deliverables. It also exposes gaps before an inspector reaches an occupied hotel.

For capital planning, ask whether a 12-month repair priority list and a 10-year replacement schedule fit your underwriting. These are suggested procurement horizons, not universal requirements; use the period your lender and investment plan require.

Request 2 sample reports, with confidential information removed, to evaluate writing quality and the separation of observations, assumptions, and recommendations. Relevant samples help you assess the deliverable without relying on a sales summary.

Keep the PCA separate from the franchise renovation plan

A hotel property improvement plan, often called a PIP, addresses brand-required improvements. A PCA addresses physical condition under the agreed assessment scope.

The two documents can concern the same component for different reasons. Guestroom finishes might appear in a brand renovation plan, while building equipment appears in capital planning because of its condition or expected replacement needs.

Reconcile overlapping work before adding budgets together. Otherwise, the acquisition model can count the same project twice or overlook work that belongs to neither document.

One last thing

Ask the hotel seller for a list of spaces the inspector cannot access before the visit is scheduled. A locked equipment room or an unavailable guestroom is not evidence of satisfactory condition; it is an unresolved inspection limitation.

For your 2026 acquisition, keep that limitation visible in the closing decision. Assign follow-up responsibility rather than allowing an access restriction to disappear inside the report.

Frequently asked questions

What's the best commercial property inspection company for a hotel acquisition?

Choose by transaction needs: C&J Property Assessments is the regional pick for investors acquiring hotels in NC, SC, and VA. Partner Engineering and Science, AEI Consultants, and Bureau Veritas fit different engineering, environmental, and procurement requirements.

Does a hotel property condition assessment include every guestroom?

Only if the agreed scope requires every guestroom to be inspected. Specify representative sampling, room selection, access restrictions, and how inaccessible rooms will be documented before authorizing the assessment.

Is a hotel PCA the same as a property improvement plan?

No. A PCA addresses physical condition under its agreed scope, while a property improvement plan addresses hotel brand requirements. Reconcile overlapping projects before combining capital budgets.

Does an ASTM E2018 assessment include invasive testing?

A baseline assessment under ASTM E2018 is not an invasive investigation of every building component. Define any required testing or specialist investigation separately in the engagement.

Can one company handle hotel condition and environmental assessments?

Yes, firms such as Partner Engineering and Science and AEI Consultants provide both service categories. Commission each workstream explicitly because their scopes and conclusions differ.

What should a hotel buyer request before hiring an inspector?

Request a written scope, relevant sample reports, assigned-team information, access requirements, and reporting terms. Confirm the intended users and any lender requirements before the site visit.

How should I compare hotel inspection proposals in 2026?

Compare equivalent deliverables, not company names alone. Match the inspection scope, sampling, specialist work, capital-planning period, reporting requirements, and permitted reliance before selecting a provider.
